cell_type_context: Primary human naive B cells from normal and STAT3-, IL21R- or IL2RG-mutant donors; CD40L plus IL-21 stimulation; IL2RA expression, STAT3 ChIP and CD25/plasmablast readouts
compartment_context: IL21R:IL2RG receptor complex to JAK1/JAK3 cytoplasmic relay and STAT3-dependent IL2RA promoter regulation
injury_context: no SCI transfer inferred; human B-cell differentiation model only
context_scope: direct primary target-gene evidence; receptor-reconstituted and primary immune-cell contexts remain bounded
assay_or_perturbation: IL-21 stimulation, STAT3 loss-of-function donor comparison, STAT3 chromatin immunoprecipitation and IL2RA expression assays
citation_note: Primary study reports IL-21 induction of IL2RA/CD25 in human naive B cells, loss of induction with STAT3, IL21R or IL2RG mutation, and STAT3 ChIP at IL2RA; primary locator: PMID:24159173; PMCID:PMC3854113
evidence_summary: Primary-supported claim: IL-21 signaling through IL21R/IL2RG induces IL2RA/CD25 through STAT3 in human naive B cells. The study shows impaired IL2RA induction in STAT3-, IL21R- and IL2RG-mutant cells and direct STAT3 occupancy at the IL2RA locus. This evidence-layer route links the existing IL21 receptor/JAK/STAT3 evidence to a target-gene output without asserting universal cytokine behavior, SCI transfer or causal graph traversal.
limitations: Human CD40L-stimulated naive B-cell context; IL2RA is a direct target in this model, but the route remains evidence-only and does not imply that all IL-21-responsive cells use the same terminal output. No database confidence score is asserted.

cell_type_context: RAW264.7 cells and mouse bone-marrow-derived macrophages; LPS with or without exogenous IL-10; IL1RN promoter activity and mRNA assays
compartment_context: IL10RA:IL10RB receptor complex to JAK1/TYK2 and STAT3-dependent IL1RN promoter regulation
injury_context: no SCI transfer inferred; mouse macrophage inflammatory model only
context_scope: direct primary target-gene evidence; IL-10 effect is stimulus-dependent and retained with its LPS co-stimulation qualifier
assay_or_perturbation: IL-10 plus LPS stimulation, IL1RN promoter reporter, dominant-negative STAT3, promoter STAT3-site analysis and IL-10-deficient macrophage rescue
citation_note: Primary study shows IL-10 enhancement of LPS-induced IL1RN promoter activity and mRNA through a functional STAT3-binding site; primary locator: PMID:15218058; DOI:10.1189/jlb.1003526
evidence_summary: Primary-supported claim: IL-10 enhances LPS-induced IL1RN/IL-1 receptor antagonist transcription in mouse macrophage systems through STAT3-dependent promoter activity. Dominant-negative STAT3 inhibits the response, and the promoter contains a functional STAT3-binding site. This evidence-layer route adds a target-gene output to the existing IL-10 receptor/JAK/STAT3 evidence while preserving the LPS co-stimulation requirement.
limitations: The IL1RN response is strongest in the LPS-plus-IL-10 context and should not be generalized to IL-10 alone in every cell type. No SCI transfer, causal graph traversal or database confidence score is asserted.

citation_note: Primary study reports IL-15-dependent anti-apoptotic signaling requiring IL-15Rbeta, JAK3 and STAT5, with BCL2/BCL2L1-associated survival output; primary locator: PMID:20440074
evidence_summary: Primary-supported claim: IL-15 signaling through IL-15Rbeta/common-gamma requires JAK3 and STAT5 for anti-apoptotic BCL2/BCL2L1-associated survival of human intraepithelial lymphocytes. The study uses IL-15 blockade and pathway measurements to connect receptor stimulation, JAK3/STAT5 activation and survival output. The target-gene identity and direct STAT5 promoter linkage remain unasserted, so this is retained as a partial route rather than a full target-gene chain.
limitations: Human intestinal IEL and refractory-celiac-disease context; BCL2/BCL2L1 are reported as anti-apoptotic outputs but not promoted here as a direct STAT5 target-gene edge. Preserve IL15RA/trans-presentation and cis-signaling distinctions from the receptor evidence. No SCI transfer or database confidence score is asserted.
